candidates.attacker_control: An authenticated user sends POST /api/2/search/search?siteId=<site> with an attacker-chosen JSON SearchParams body (keywords/query/filters; `path` is only an optional inclusive filter, never a restricting one). The default blueprint permission mappings grant `content_search` to every site role (author/publisher/reviewer/developer/admin) on the catch-all rule, so any site member can invoke it. The user only needs to control the query terms; the result set is the whole `<siteId>-authoring*` index.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that the query parameter path (SearchParams.path) is only an optional caller-supplied regexp filter and does not restrict results; verified no later post-filtering by permissions in SearchServiceInternalImpl.processResults/processSearchHit; verified the class really is the wired implementation (`authoringSearchService` in studio-search-context.xml) used by SearchServiceImpl; verified the sibling method explicitly throws to prevent unfiltered parameterized searches, confirming the intended invariant; verified site-level @HasPermission(content_search) exists but is not a path-level check; considered that the empty allowedPaths may reflect a known-incomplete feature (TODOs), which is why confidence is medium rather than high; verified the index selection uses the validated siteId, so this is intra-site, not cross-tenant.
candidates.impact: Authorization/information-disclosure: an authenticated site user can obtain search hits (content paths plus highlighted content snippets and metadata) for content in the site they do not have path-level `content_read` permission for, bypassing the path granularity of Crafter's permission model. Severity is highest on installations that use path-restricted permission mappings and index sensitive files (e.g. configuration files under /config with credentials/keys); it does not cross site boundaries because the index name is derived from the supplied siteId (itself validated).
candidates.prerequisites: Authentication plus the site-level `content_search` permission (granted by default to all standard roles). Impact requires the site to use path-scoped `content_read` mappings that restrict some roles to subtrees (customized permission-mappings-config.xml) and/or indexed files outside the user's readable subtrees (e.g. configuration/content the engine indexer indexed). No special privileges or victim interaction needed.
candidates.root_cause: PermissionAwareSearchService is wired into the authoring search pipeline to restrict results by the requesting user's allowed paths, but its `search(String siteId, SearchRequest, Class)` method always passes `allowedPaths = emptyList()` with the TODO `Get allowed paths from the security service`, and `getRequestUpdates()` only calls `addFilters()` when `allowedPaths` is non-empty, so the OpenSearch query is executed with no path-permission filter. The sibling overload `search(SearchRequest, Class, Map)` throws UnsupportedOperationException to 'Prevent execution of requests without permission filters', but the used overload is exactly such an execution. SearchServiceImpl only enforces the site-level `content_search` permission; its injected `securityService` (and `siteService`) fields are unused, indicating the permission/allow-list logic that was expected around search is absent. The search context XML wires the permission-aware service without any security service provider.
candidates.title: Search results are not filtered by path permissions (missing authorization filter in PermissionAwareSearchService)
candidates.trace: SearchController.search → SearchServiceImpl.search (@HasPermission(PERMISSION_CONTENT_SEARCH) site-level only; injected securityService/siteService unused) → ClausesLimitAwareSearchService.search → SearchServiceInternalImpl.search builds the query from user keywords/query/filters (only adds params.getPath() when the caller supplies it) → PermissionAwareSearchService.search(siteId, request, Map.class) is invoked at SearchServiceInternalImpl:569; that method sets allowedPaths=emptyList() and calls super.search(request, documentClass, Map.of("siteId", siteId, "allowedPaths", allowedPaths)); AbstractOpenSearchClientWrapper then calls the overridden getRequestUpdates, which sets the index and executes `if (CollectionUtils.isNotEmpty(allowedPaths)) { addFilters(...) }`; because allowedPaths is empty, no regexp path filters are attached and the query executes unfiltered over the site authoring index; hits are mapped into SearchResultItem with path, name, last editor, size, mime type and highlight snippets (studio.search.fields.highlight includes content/*_html/*_txt) and returned to the attacker.
candidates.unverified: I could not confirm which upstream commit fixed this or whether the missing allow-list is the specific benchmark vulnerability. I did not verify (and cannot from source alone) whether the engine indexer actually indexes files outside normal content paths in a given deployment, nor whether the affected sites commonly configure path-scoped content_read rules; both affect real-world exploitation. I also could not execute anything to observe the returned results.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization (missing per-path content authorization in search)

coverage_summary: Scope: 1249 model-visible files under the assigned source root (Crafter Studio 4.3.0-SNAPSHOT), with the tools' standard filters (binary-like files skipped, 5 MiB per-file text limit, sensitive-name/symlink exclusions reported as zero). I inspected the Spring security configuration (api.xml/web.xml/common.xml/studio-config.yaml), all v2 REST controllers, v2/v1 service implementations for content, configuration, search, security/users/groups, workflow, publish, repository/git, AWS S3/MediaConvert, WebDAV, marketplace/plugins, proxy, scripting, policy validators, MyBatis mappers, the legacy Groovy v1 REST scripts and their Spring-backed implementations, and the upgrade/XXE-sensitive parsers. Coverage is source-level only and was driven by targeted searches (exec/ProcessBuilder, XML parsers, path/File APIs, MyBatis ${} interpolation, permission annotations, @Validate* annotations, request-parameter handling), so unsearched corners (e.g. some webapp static assets, blueprint content, and parts of large impl classes) were not exhaustively line-read.
limitations: No execution, build, decompilation, or dependency-jar inspection was possible, so crafter-commons annotations/validators (ValidExistingContentPath, ValidConfigurationPath, ValidateSecurePathParam, SqlSort) and external classes (AbstractOpenSearchClientWrapper, JGit TreeWalk) were reasoned about from usage only.

No repository history, fix commits, tests, or external CVE data were available, so I could not confirm the intended ground-truth vulnerability; the candidate is a source-evidence lead, not a runtime-confirmed finding.
Impact of the search candidate depends on deployment configuration (path-scoped content_read mappings and what the engine indexer indexes), which is not fully determined by this repository.

Several other plausible leads (item-states regex path, getGitPath backslash normalization, XmlFileVersionProvider XXE, externally-managed group membership) were kept as rejected because reachability or impact could not be established from the visible source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Command/argument injection in ImageMagickTransformer (Runtime.getRuntime().exec(cmdLine) with options from site asset-processing config).
rejected_leads.reason: Runtime.exec(String) does not invoke a shell, so metacharacter command execution is not possible (at most ImageMagick-specific argument/file-write abuse), and the options value comes from a configuration file requiring write_configuration privileges; no clear unauthenticated or cross-boundary impact was established.

rejected_leads.lead: Regex/allow-list mismatch in WorkflowController.getItemStates path used both for permission lookup (path.matches(regex)) and for a DB RLIKE filter.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible authorization bypass (a path string that fully matches an allow rule can also be a broader regexp in the DAO), but it depends on unverifiable crafter-commons validator semantics and on whether internal MethodValidationPostProcessor checks apply to SecurityServiceImpl (class is not @Validated), so it did not reach the evidence bar.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal via GitRepositoryHelper.getGitPath (normalize before separatorsToUnix leaves backslash-based '..' segments), feeding Path.resolve/FileInputStream in shallow content operations.
rejected_leads.reason: The dangerous normalization order is visible, but I could not show an attacker-reachable API that reaches a shallow read/write with an unvalidated path; @ValidateSecurePathParam/@ValidConfigurationPath annotations may block the needed characters, and non-shallow Git reads go through JGit TreeWalk which rejects dot segments.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in XmlFileVersionProvider (SAXReader without disallow-doctype-decl/external-entity features) and in DocumentHelper.parseText call sites.
rejected_leads.reason: The parser hardening is missing, but reachability is limited to upgrade/version-provider code paths operating on repository files, and the parsed result is not clearly returned to an attacker; impact could not be established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Externally-managed group membership can be modified via /api/2/groups/{id}/members (checkExternallyManagedGroup is called for update/delete but not for add/remove members).
rejected_leads.reason: Real inconsistency in new 2025 groups code, but it requires the already-powerful update_groups permission, and the security impact (versus intended IdP sync behavior) is speculative.

rejected_leads.lead: Unused injectable parameters on internal service impls because they are not @Validated (e.g. @ValidateSecurePathParam/@ValidateStringParam constraints are not enforced for internal calls such as SecurityServiceImpl.getUserPermissions).
rejected_leads.reason: Systemic hardening gap rather than a single exploitable root cause; endpoints are protected by controller-level validation, and no concrete end-to-end exploit was traced.

summary: Reviewed the Crafter Studio 4.3.0-SNAPSHOT source tree (1249 files): REST controllers, security/permission resolution, content/item/search services, repository/blob store code, legacy Groovy v1 API scripts, MyBatis mappers, and XML/HTML/Groovy config. Path-parameter validation, permission annotations, and XML parser hardening are present in most places, but the search path-permission filter appears to be missing: `PermissionAwareSearchService` is explicitly designed to add per-path permission filters (`allowedPaths`, `pathFieldName`, `addFilters`) and even refuses the parameterized overload without filters, yet the production call path supplies an empty `allowedPaths` list and then skips filtering entirely. Any authenticated user with the site-level `content_search` permission can therefore query the whole site authoring index and receive paths/metadata/highlighted content snippets without per-path `content_read` filtering. I submit this single candidate; other plausible but weaker/unverified leads are listed as rejected.
